chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar or to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: 'The fasting of three days in the month—I delay it in the summer until the winter, for I find it easier upon me then.'
So he said: 'Yes, but preserve it.'

key_terms.أَهْوَنَ: easier; less difficult for the one observing the fast
key_terms.الشَّهْرِ: the month; indicating the regular recurring practice
key_terms.الشِّتَاءِ: winter; the season to which the fasting is postponed for ease
key_terms.الصَّيْفِ: summer; the season from which the fasting is being delayed
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: three days; the monthly recommended number of fast days
key_terms.صَوْمُ: fasting; here, the recommended fasting practice being discussed
key_terms.فَاحْفَظْهَا: so preserve it; meaning to keep up and not abandon this observance

ai.seo_question: Can the recommended three fast days of the month be postponed from summer to winter?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility of delaying the recommended fast of three days each month from summer to winter when that is easier for the person. At the same time, the Imam عليه السلام emphasizes that the practice should still be maintained and not neglected altogether.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1795 - It is narrated by al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
"I said to Abu Ja‘far or Abu Abdullah (as): 'Can I delay fasting the three days of the month in the summer until the winter, as I find it easier for me then?'
Imam (as) said: 'Yes, but make sure to observe it.'"
